clue.text: The bridge party's objectives causing confused talk …

definitions.meaning: the aims of people going over a bridge, read literally
talking at odds, each side misunderstanding the other

explanation.surface: Card players at a bridge evening argue at length about what they are each trying to achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge party' looks like a card game; read it as people crossing a bridge. The ellipsis runs the clue on into 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Two parties misunderstanding each other's aims are said to be at odds in exactly this way, and their muddled talk is the idiom.

clue.text: Ready-money pool helping fend off the cold

definitions.note: describes a warm material rather than naming it

parts.note: ready money is cash in hand
a mere is a small lake or pool

explanation.surface: A fund of spare money is set aside to pay the heating bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine goat wool woven into jumpers and scarves keeps the wearer warm in winter.

clue.text: Go beyond what's reasonable in taking another's part

definitions.text: Go beyond what's reasonable in taking another's part

parts.words: Go beyond what's reasonable in taking another's part
parts.note: reads like defending a friend too zealously, but describes an actor playing a role with too much exaggeration

explanation.surface: Someone sticks up for a friend in an argument and goes too far.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor playing a role with excessive emphasis is exaggerating the performance beyond what is natural.

clue.text: In South America the monkey told some nifty stories, but …

definitions.meaning: a long-tailed monkey of South American forests
the pen name of H. H. Munro, writer of witty short stories

explanation.surface: A monkey in South America spins clever tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 5 down, but this clue is complete as a double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a bushy-tailed Amazonian primate and to the Edwardian short-story writer famous for sharp, witty tales.

clue.text: See 1
… nimble accounts turned into black North American tragedy

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are turned about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lively stories are turned into a tragic tale of North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned into' rearranges the fourteen letters of NIMBLE ACCOUNTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Beecher Stowe's anti-slavery novel tells the tragic story of an enslaved Black man in America.

clue.text: Seedy, but just wins

definitions.meaning: read as full of small seeds, as of fruit stones
to beat by a whisker, as in winning at the post

explanation.surface: A shabby person who nonetheless scrapes a narrow victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedy' looks like shabby; here it means having seeds, pointing to fruit seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fruit seeds share the name with narrowly beating a rival in a race.

clue.text: Everything in the display is superficial

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other here

parts.note: a show is a display
all means everything

explanation.surface: A complaint that a whole exhibition lacks depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking depth, both of water and of thought, is the sense shared.

clue.text: A description of some beachcomber's hue?

definitions.text: A description of some beachcomber's hue?

parts.words: A description of some beachcomber's hue?
parts.note: a beachcomber may be coloured by the beach itself, or have hair the shade of the shore

explanation.surface: Wondering what colour a beach scavenger might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish-brown colour like a beach, used especially of reddish-blond hair.

clue.text: Cowardly hit resulting from a momentary confrontation

definitions.meaning: a hit by Noel Coward, the 1945 film from his play

explanation.surface: A cowardly punch thrown during a brief scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cowardly' looks like timid; it means by Noel Coward, the English playwright whose play became this famous film.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward's short play filmed by David Lean has a title meaning a short meeting, so both senses fit.

clue.text: … for this head of the house

definitions.text: for this head of the house

parts.words: for this head of the house
parts.note: continues 1 across: confused talk is a trouble for the person who chairs the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Muddled debate is a headache for whoever presides over the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens with an ellipsis: read it after 1 across, whose confused talk is the problem for this person.
explanation.definitionFit: The presiding officer of the House of Commons is the head of that house, keeping order in debate.

clue.text: Cook was making arrangements for eleven

definitions.text: Cook was making arrangements for eleven

parts.words: Cook was making arrangements for eleven
parts.note: James Cook held this naval rank, and a cricket team of eleven is led by one who sets the field

explanation.surface: A chef is preparing a dinner for eleven guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a chef; it is James Cook the explorer. Eleven is a cricket or football side, whose leader arranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The explorer held this rank, and the leader of a sports team is given the same title.

clue.text: Bully's sphere may finally dwindle to it

definitions.text: Bully's sphere may finally dwindle to it

parts.words: Bully's sphere may finally dwindle to it
parts.note: bully beef is canned corned beef, and a sphere of it is a small round of minced beef

explanation.surface: A bully's area of influence might eventually shrink to nothing much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' looks like a tormentor; it is bully beef, the British name for canned corned beef. 'Sphere' is a round shape, not a domain.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round of minced beef, the shape a sphere of bully beef would take.

clue.text: How many, world wonders, Poles kept apart by woman?

indicators.note: the two poles are separated, with the woman standing between them

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
Eve, the first woman

explanation.surface: Asking how many Polish visitors a woman kept apart from each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the two poles of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient world listed a number of wonders, from the Pyramids to the Colossus: that count.

clue.text: A manoeuvre to pull at the oars around duck

indicators.note: the rowing word goes around the duck

parts.note: to ply is to work steadily, as at the oars
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Rowing round a duck on the river as a tactical move.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning move or tactic designed to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Instant joy is far-fetched, you'll discover initially

indicators.note: the first letters of the following words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A promise that quick happiness lies far off, as you'll find out.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment, as in 'back in a tick'.

clue.text: Corner gangleader in winding lane

indicators.note: the gang's first letter goes inside the reworked lane
a winding lane twists, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the leader of a gang is its first letter, G; that the run ... also sits inside this word is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A gang boss is cornered in a twisting lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges LANE to ANLE, and 'in' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two lines or walls meet at a point, as in a corner.

clue.text: Reporter running his own paper shop?

definitions.text: Reporter running his own paper shop?

parts.words: Reporter running his own paper shop?
parts.note: a reporter sells news; so does a newsagent, who runs a shop selling papers

explanation.surface: A journalist who also runs a newsagent's.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling goods is a trader, and one selling news is a reporter.

clue.text: Passed on, deed! Case is bust!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Passed on, indeed! Case is bust!': the parse is DE(CEAS)ED, CASE rearranged inside DEED, so 'indeed' gives both the container indicator 'in' and the fodder DEED: one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Passed on, deed! Case is bust!

clue.text: You'd not hear a fixer fall for such utter hush-hush conditions

definitions.text: You'd not hear a fixer fall for such utter hush-hush conditions

parts.words: You'd not hear a fixer fall for such utter hush-hush conditions
parts.note: a fixer is a pin; you could hear a pin drop in total quiet

explanation.surface: In secret conditions you would never notice a corrupt operator being brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fixer fall' is a pin drop: the idiom 'you could hear a pin drop' describes total quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute quiet, with no sound at all, is the state described.

clue.text: The growth of paperwork in Spain

definitions.text: The growth of paperwork in Spain

parts.words: The growth of paperwork in Spain
parts.note: reads as spreading bureaucracy, but means a grass grown in Spain and used to make paper

explanation.surface: Complaining about mounting Spanish bureaucracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough grass of Spain and North Africa, used for rope and paper making.

clue.text: Carefully managing to train brothers to mix gins

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, whose members called each other brothers

indicators.note: the gins are mixed, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bartenders training their brothers to mix gin drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to mix' rearranges GINS to SING. The NUR was a British trade union for railway workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending something with care, as one tends a grievance or a lead.

clue.text: Manage a musical composition in church

indicators.note: the composition sits inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
op. is short for opus, a numbered musical work

explanation.surface: Organising a piece of music in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal successfully with something difficult, to get by.

clue.text: One poem among 400 needs deciphering

indicators.note: the poem is placed among the letters of the number

parts.note: CD is 400 in Roman numerals
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A single poem in a collection of four hundred is hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Written in cipher, a message must be decoded before it can be read.

clue.text: Jade's true growth producing rose colours

indicators.note: these letters grow into a new arrangement, producing the answer

explanation.surface: A green gemstone that truly grows and turns pink.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree said to be where Judas hanged himself bears purple-pink blossoms in spring.

clue.text: See 23
See 12
Box-spring given poor finish

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: the finish of poor is its last letter

explanation.surface: A mattress spring box that has a poor end.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice.

clue.text: Though out of the dorm, Anthea's still asleep it seems

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the letters running through these words

explanation.surface: Though Anthea has left the dormitory she seems still to be asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive, as if sleeping; a volcano at rest is described this way.

clue.text: Damages given to one million couples

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
pairs are couples

explanation.surface: Damages awarded to a millionaire.
explanation.definitionFit: Weakens or harms, as noise harms hearing.

clue.text: Display of jest made Cockney cry in thirsty conditions

indicators.note: the cry goes inside the thirsty word

parts.note: dry means without drink
a Cockney drops the h, so holler becomes 'oller

explanation.surface: A joke that made a Londoner shout in a drought.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney, a working-class Londoner, drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Comical, whimsical humour: a display of wit.

clue.text: Deranged Den taken out showed violence

indicators.note: the letters of den are removed

explanation.surface: A lunatic named Den is removed after a rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: D, E and N are removed from DERANGED, scattered but in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormed furiously, as a fire or a tempest does.
